Commentary.Commentary: Back for the chase. The players are out in the middle. Brian Bennett and Tadiwanashe Marumani to open for Zimbabwe. Gerhard Erasmus to bowl first.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

But Ruben Trumpelmann stepped up, unleashing a whirlwind 46 off 24 balls, taking Zimbabwe's bowlers to task. His cameo provided the much-needed late acceleration for Namibia. Alexander Volschenk finished the innings in style, smashing an unbeaten 20 off 11 balls, including a big six. Namibia posted 204/7 in their 20 overs, thanks to some scintillating batting from Frylinck and Trumpelmann. Can Zimbabwe chase down this total? We'll have to wait and see.

And what an innings it was for Namibia! Jan Frylinck was on fire from the get-go, smashing his fifty off just 13 balls, a record for the fastest fifty by a Namibian player. He and debutant Louren Steenkamp put on 74 runs for the opening wicket, with Frylinck going on to score 77 before being trapped by Sikandar Raza. That breakthrough was crucial for Zimbabwe, but Namibia's middle order faltered, slumping to 144/6. Gerhard Erasmus, Jan Nicol Loftie-Eaton, JJ Smit, and Zane Green couldn't capitalize on their starts.
SIX! What a shot to end the innings! Short, on leg, Alexander Volschenk swivels and pulls it over fine leg for a biggie. Namibia end their innings at 204/7!

Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza stated that his team preferred bowling first. Raza highlighted three changes in the lineups. He emphasized that confidence stems from good performances, citing Zimbabwe's recent success against Sri Lanka. Currently leading the series 2-0, Raza stressed the importance of taking each game one at a time, given the cutthroat nature of the qualifier.

Namibia captain Gerhard Erasmus says that his team will bat first. He revealed two changes in the lineup, expressing excitement for the match and praising the series for providing valuable exposure for young players. Erasmus commended Zimbabwe's skills, noting they've posed significant challenges for Namibia throughout the series.

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Brian Bennett, Tadiwanashe Marumani, Brendan Taylor (WK), Sean Williams (In for Brad Evans), Sikandar Raza (C), Ryan Burl, Tashinga Musekiwa, Wellington Masakadza, Tinotenda Maposa, Blessing Muzarabani (In for Richard Ngarava), Trevor Gwandu (In for Trevor Gwandu).

TOSS - Namibia have won the toss and will BAT first.

Now, as we head into the final match, the stakes are different for both teams. Namibia, having lost the series, will be playing for pride and a chance to salvage a win against a strong opponent. Meanwhile, Zimbabwe will be focused on a ruthless performance to cap off their successful campaign with a clean sweep. Get ready for a thrilling contest as these two teams give it their all in Bulawayo! Toss and team news to follow shortly...

However, Zimbabwe's chase was once again anchored by the impressive Tadiwanashe Marumani, who notched his third consecutive T20I fifty. Ryan Burl’s late heroics with the bat sealed the win, proving that the Chevrons have the depth and firepower to chase down challenging totals. Their consistent performance has been a testament to their form and determination throughout the series.

The series so far has been a showcase of explosive batting and tense finishes. In the opener, the Chevrons' top order, led by spectacular fifties from Brian Bennett and Tadiwanashe Marumani, posted a formidable total of 211. Despite a valiant chase from the Namibian Eagles, Zimbabwe's bowlers, particularly Blessing Muzarabani and Sikandar Raza, held their nerve to secure a 33-run victory. The second match saw Namibia put up a strong total of 169, thanks to some fine contributions from Malan Kruger, Nicol Loftie-Eaton, and captain Gerhard Erasmus.

Welcome to the final showdown of the three-match T20I series between Zimbabwe and Namibia! The stage is set at Queens Sports Club in Bulawayo for what promises to be an exciting conclusion. The home side, Zimbabwe, comes into this match with an unassailable 2-0 lead, having already clinched the series with two impressive performances. They'll be looking to complete a clean sweep and assert their dominance with a memorable whitewash on their home turf.
...MATCH DAY...

The third and final T20I at Queens Sports Club may be a dead rubber in the series scoreline, but not in spirit. Zimbabwe already have the trophy bagged with a 2-0 lead, and now they eye a whitewash to stamp their authority. For Namibia, this match is about pride, resilience, and avoiding the bitter taste of a clean sweep. After back-to-back games in two consecutive days that tested both teams’ depth, a day’s breather gives both sides a chance to recharge before one final push. So, how have Zimbabwe played so far? Quite brilliantly. Their batting has been on fire, where Brian Bennett has been the standout star, smashing 94 in the first game and a fiery 40 off just 20 balls in the second, making him the series’ batting heartbeat. Tadiwanashe Marumani, too, has been consistent, following his 62 in the opener with a quickfire 50 in the second. Add in Brendan Taylor’s calm and Ryan Burl’s late fireworks, and the top and middle order look in perfect sync. The bowling has done its job as well, with Richard Ngarava and Brad Evans picking up crucial wickets, while Sikandar Raza continues to chip in with both bat and ball. Then, is there anything that Zimbabwe need to improve? Their bowling - which has been good but in patches. In the first game, Namibia’s late-order hitting dented their death overs. In the second, despite chasing comfortably, they did allow Namibia’s middle order to build partnerships. With the series done, Zimbabwe might even test their bench strength, but Raza will want his attack to be sharper, especially in containing power hitters like Jan Nicol Loftie-Eaton and Gerhard Erasmus. Meanwhile, on the flip side, we have Namibia. Where do they stand after two tough outings? They’ve shown spirit but lacked finishing. In the opener, Jan Nicol Loftie-Eaton and Zane Green gave them hope, but chasing a target of 212 was always uphill. In the second game, they were much better - Malan Kruger, Loftie-Eaton, and Erasmus all stitched together a competitive 169, only to watch Zimbabwe hunt it down with ease. The bowlers, led by JJ Smit and Ruben Trumpelmann, fought hard but couldn’t keep Zimbabwe’s aggressive top order quiet. So, what do Namibia need to do to finally cross the line? Convert starts into a match-winning innings. Loftie-Eaton and Kruger have looked good but haven’t carried through to the 70s or 80s that can tilt games. Erasmus needs more support from the lower middle order, where Smit and Trumpelmann can play bigger roles. Bowling-wise, Namibia must strike early - dismissing Bennett or Marumani inside the powerplay is key. Otherwise, they’ll be left chasing shadows again. So, what’s the buildup for this final clash? The Bulawayo pitch has been friendly for batters, with both games crossing 160 easily. Expect another high-scoring contest where the new ball holds the key and slower balls at the death will decide the margins. Zimbabwe, riding on form and home advantage, look favourite to complete the whitewash. But Namibia, with pride on the line and no pressure of series results, might just throw caution to the wind and play their freest cricket yet. Will Zimbabwe complete a clean sweep to underline their dominance, or can Namibia roar back and snatch one for pride? The answer comes under the Bulawayo skies.
